newsitem.title: USA: A.M. Best downgrades First Central to "D".
newsitem.headline: A.M. Best downgrades First Central to "D".

text.p: A.M Best Co said Wednesday it had downgraded First Central Insurance Co to a "D" or "very vulnerable" rating from a secure "B++" or "very good" rating.

Best said the downgrade is based on the substantial deterioration of First Central's financial condition and follows the February 14 announcement that the company will take a $11.5 million charge to earnings to raise its loss reserves.
The reserve shortfall, which relates to the company's 1995 carried reserves, is currently under review by the New York Insurance Department, Best said.
Best said the downgrade reflects its concerns over First Central's diminished capitalization and financial flexibility and inability to service debt of its parent, First Central Financial Corp.

Best said that as a result of the extraordinary reserve additions, the company's 1996 year-end statutory surplus is expected to plummet more than 60 percent from the prior year, to about $10.5 million.
First Central will not be able to pay any dividents to its parent, it said.
It said the Lynbrook, N.Y.,-based company has about $5 million of convertible subordinated debentures outstanding with interest and sinking fund obligations of $2 million due to be paid in August."
Failure to pay the obligations will constitute default, it said.
